title: CISSP vs CompTIA Security+: Which Do You Need?
subtitle: First security cert or senior cert — which one is right for you?

pros: The standard entry-level cert — recognized by virtually every junior security recruiter.
No experience prerequisite to sit the exam.
90-minute exam, mostly multiple choice — predictable preparation.
A DoD 8570/8140 baseline — required for many US government / contractor roles.
A natural bridge to CySA+, PenTest+, and later the CISSP.
cons: A low ceiling — few employers go much beyond entry-level pay on Security+ alone (rarely above €50k in France).
Breadth over depth: covers everything, masters nothing in depth.
Less recognized in Europe than in the US.
certs.bestFor: You're starting out in security, you don't have 5 years of experience, and you want to land your first job.

pros: The most recognized security cert worldwide.
Senior median salary of €80-95k in France, €110-130k in Switzerland/Luxembourg (Hays 2026).
Opens the door to CISO and Security Architect roles.
International recognition — helps with mobility to the US/UK/Canada.
cons: 5 years of documented security experience required for the full cert (without it, you become an 'Associate of ISC2').
$749 for the exam + a $125 annual maintenance fee.
3-hour adaptive exam, 100-150 questions — 300-500 hours of prep if you're starting from a thin base.
Covers 8 very broad domains — not a hyper-technical, hands-on cert.
certs.bestFor: You have 4-5 years of security/IT experience and are targeting a senior role (CISO, security architect, audit).

verdicts.profile: You're starting your career (0-2 years of experience).
verdicts.why: The CISSP requires 5 years of experience — without it you only get the 'Associate' status, which doesn't convince recruiters.

verdicts.profile: You have 5+ years of security/IT experience and are targeting CISO / Architect / senior roles.
verdicts.why: It is the cert that unlocks these titles. Unmatched ROI at the senior end of the pay scale.

verdicts.profile: You're looking for a DoD or US contractor role.
verdicts.why: A DoD 8570/8140 baseline — required to get in. The CISSP is required later for senior positions.

verdicts.profile: You don't have the budget for a $749 exam + 200-300 hours of study.
verdicts.why: A reasonable investment ($392, ~120 hours). You can take the CISSP later once you have your 5 years.

verdicts.profile: You already work as a security analyst and want a significant raise.
verdicts.why: The CISSP salary jump is documented: €15-25k in France according to Hays 2026, more in Switzerland/Luxembourg.

tldr: Security+ if you're starting out (and you don't have a choice — the CISSP requires 5 years of experience). CISSP if you have 5+ years and are targeting senior pay.
